tagline: Leading Finnish bank providing comprehensive banking and financial services to private and corporate customers
hero_kpi_rationale: Aktia's primary revenue comes from net interest income (korkokate), which represents over half of its total revenue and is the main driver of its financial performance
company_description: Aktia Pankki Oyj, together with its subsidiaries, provides banking and financing solutions in Finland. It operates through four segments: Asset Management, Banking Business, Life Insurance, and Group Functions. The company offers banking services, including savings; fixed income, equity, and alternative investments; leisure, investment, and reverse mortgages; construction, investment, unsecured consumer, ASP, student, and green loans; secured consumer credit; and life, disability, critical illness, and group pension insurance products. It also provides investment, asset, and wealth management; business, customer funds, and currency accounts, as well as savings deposit; payment transactions; cards; online services; and financing services, such as bank guarantee, installment, leasing, and factoring. In addition, the company offers financing and liquidity management; sales assistance; and IT and product support and development. It serves individuals, corporate customers, and institutions. The company was formerly known as Aktia Savings Bank Plc, Banking Services and changed its name to Aktia Pankki Oyj in March 2008. Aktia Pankki Oyj was founded in 1825 and is headquartered in Helsinki

kpis.name: Net Interest Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest income received and interest expenses paid.
kpis.description: Net interest income increased by EUR 152.0 million due to stronger interest margins and higher benchmark rates, driven by growth in loan interest income (+20%) and liquidity portfolio income (+51%).
kpis.signal: Sustained growth supported by higher interest rates.

kpis.name: Net Fee Income
kpis.explanation: Revenue from banking service fees such as cards and asset management.
kpis.description: Driven by growth in average customer assets (+2%) and fund activities, reaching EUR 124.3 million.

kpis.name: Comparable Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Comparable operating profit rose strongly to EUR 124.5 million despite a decline in reported profit, reflecting improved cost control.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement due to better cost discipline.

kpis.name: Personnel Expenses
kpis.explanation: Total cost related to employees, including salaries and benefits.
kpis.description: Comparable personnel expenses decreased to EUR 80.5 million due to headcount reduction and lower one-off expenses, partially offset by higher capitalization of development costs.
kpis.signal: Cost reduction driven by lower headcount (FTE).

kpis.name: IT Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs related to IT systems, infrastructure, and digital projects.
kpis.description: IT expenses increased to EUR 51.5 million due to continued investments in banking systems, payment infrastructure, and asset management, as well as inflationary effects.
kpis.signal: Sharp increase linked to investments in IT infrastructure and modernization.

kpis.name: Life Insurance Net Result
kpis.explanation: Profitability of life insurance operations after claims and expenses.
kpis.description: Life insurance result improved significantly to EUR 30.2 million, driven by premium portfolio growth, lower claims incidence, and better investment performance in insurance and asset portfolios.
kpis.signal: Strong performance driven by improved claims experience and growing customer base.

kpis.name: Total Operating Costs
kpis.explanation: Sum of all operating costs of the bank.
kpis.description: Total costs increased slightly to EUR 178.6 million, despite lower personnel expenses, due to higher IT spending, absence of stability fund contribution in 2024 (compared to EUR 4.3 million in 2023), and other services.
kpis.signal: Moderate growth despite salary reductions, offset by IT increases.

risks.title: Increased Climate Regulation Risk
risks.summary: Aktia is exposed to growing climate-related regulation, particularly through EU requirements (SFDR, Taxonomy). Non-compliance could lead to penalties or loss of operating license in certain segments.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is highlighted centrally in the report, with strong emphasis on adapting to EU standards (SFDR, Taxonomy). The trend is upward due to tightening regulatory frameworks. Regulation is a strategic category for banks.

risks.title: Competition in Green Products
risks.summary: Aktia faces increasing competition in sustainable financing products, such as green loans. The risk lies in its ability to innovate and attract sustainability-conscious customers.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the development of green products in response to an evolving market. The tone is measured, but the trend is upward. Competition is a key factor in differentiating sustainable banking services.

risks.title: Dependence on External Partners for Sustainability
risks.summary: Aktia relies on external providers for emissions measurement (scope 3) and climate risk assessment. Failure or rising costs from these partners could disrupt its processes.
risks.score_rationale: Aktia depends on external partners (e.g., Green Carbon, ISS ESG) to evaluate climate impacts. The language indicates operational dependency. The trend is stable, but technological risk is moderate.

risks.title: Cybersecurity Reputational Risk
risks.summary: A cybersecurity incident could severely damage Aktia's reputation, particularly in handling sensitive customer data and sustainable investments.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly links cybersecurity to reputation, a critical point for a bank. The tone is concerned, and the risk is rising. The category is strategic due to the importance of customer data.

risks.title: Climate Transition Risk in Portfolio
risks.summary: Aktia is exposed to climate transition risks through loans to carbon-emitting companies. Sudden devaluation of these assets could impact credit portfolio quality.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is well-documented, with climate scenarios integrated into credit assessments. The language is technical and preventive. The trend is upward, reflecting growing importance of industrial risk related to transition.

risks.title: Dependence on Collective Commitments
risks.summary: Aktia relies on investor coalitions to influence companies on climate matters. The success of these actions depends on coordination with other actors, representing a strategic risk.
risks.score_rationale: Aktia participates in initiatives such as Climate Action 100+ and NZAM, implying dependence on collective action. The tone is engaged but cautious. The trend is stable, with moderate strategic impact.

risks.title: Physical Climate Change Risk
risks.summary: Real estate assets financed by Aktia are exposed to physical climate risks such as floods, potentially leading to collateral value loss.
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions exposure to physical risks (floods, extreme weather) on real estate assets. The tone is evaluative, the trend is upward. The category weight is moderate but increasing.

ai_positioning.summary: Aktia shows no clear strategy or initiative in artificial intelligence in its reports. AI mentions are absent, and IT investments appear focused on infrastructure and compliance rather than disruptive innovation.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning in the 2024 report
IT expenses are described as related to banking infrastructure and payment systems
